exposure: Trial of labor after cesarean section (TOLAC)
cohort: The study included 199 pregnant women with a history of at least one previous cesarean section from a regional teaching hospital who underwent either ERCS or TOLAC.
finding: Among women who underwent TOLAC, 86.0% had successful VBAC, with one case (2.3%) complicated by uterine rupture and neonatal death, and previous cephalo-pelvic disproportion (CPD) was associated with TOLAC failure and uterine rupture.
mod_finding: A higher VBAC success rate was found in women with previous vaginal birth (100% vs. 81.8%), and cephalo-pelvic disproportion (CPD) as an indication for previous cesarean section was associated with TOLAC failure and uterine rupture after VBAC.
